Policy Name: Cigna Lumbar Fusion (CMM-609: Lumbar Fusion with Decompression)
Referred Sections: CMM-609.7: Lumbar Fusion (with or without Decompression) Following Failed Lumbar Disc Arthroplasty Surgery

Required findings: Patient reports persistent or worsening low‑back pain and/or radicular symptoms of at least moderate intensity (≥6/10) and functional limitation despite ≥6 weeks of documented conservative therapy.

Objective physical examination demonstrates neurologic deficit correlating with the level of the arthroplasty (e.g., motor weakness, sensory loss, reflex changes) or mechanical back pain reproducible on exam.

Post‑operative imaging (plain radiographs, CT, or MRI) shows implant malposition, subsidence, loosening, dislocation, subluxation, vertebral body fracture, or other mechanical failure of the lumbar disc arthroplasty.
Conservative management has been exhausted: ≥6 weeks of physical therapy, ≥6 weeks of NSAIDs/analgesics, and/or ≥6 weeks of epidural steroid injections without sustained relief.
Patient is nicotine‑free (verified by serum, saliva, or urine cotinine test within 30 days of surgery) and has no uncontrolled behavioral health disorder that would impair postoperative recovery.
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.7: Lumbar Fusion (with or without Decompression) Following Failed Lumbar Disc Arthroplasty Surgery > Failed Lumbar Disc Arthroplasty Implant

Required findings: At least 6 months have elapsed since the index lumbar disc arthroplasty at the same level.
Patient presents with new or progressive radiculopathy, neurogenic claudication, or myelopathic symptoms unresponsive to ≥6 weeks of conservative therapy.
Objective neurologic exam reveals deficits consistent with compression at the operative level (e.g., motor weakness, sensory loss, positive straight‑leg raise, gait disturbance).

Post‑operative MRI or CT demonstrates compression of neural elements (retained disc material, recurrent herniation, osteophyte formation, or facet hypertrophy) at the level of the failed arthroplasty.
Same general criteria as above: documented trial of conservative care, nicotine‑free status confirmed by cotinine testing, and no untreated psychosocial/behavioral health issues.
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.7: Lumbar Fusion (with or without Decompression) Following Failed Lumbar Disc Arthroplasty Surgery > Evidence of Neural Structure Compression

Non-Indications: Surgery performed <6 months after the original disc arthroplasty without evidence of implant failure or neural compression.
Absence of imaging‑confirmed implant malposition/failure or neural element compression.
No documented neurologic deficit or functional impairment correlating with the level of the arthroplasty.
Failure to complete an adequate trial of conservative management (minimum 6 weeks of physical therapy, medication, and/or injections).
Active tobacco use without objective cotinine verification of cessation within 30 days of the planned procedure.
Uncontrolled psychiatric or behavioral health disorder that has not been addressed prior to surgery.
Lumbar fusion performed for pain alone without documented instability, neural compression, or implant failure.
Important criteria & exceptions: A mandatory interval of ≥6 months from the original disc arthroplasty is required for the neural compression indication.
Objective cotinine testing (serum, saliva, or urine) must be performed within 30 days of surgery; acceptable cut‑offs: serum ≤20 ng/mL, saliva ≤44 ng/mL, urine ≤10 ng/mL.
Conservative therapy must be documented in the medical record with dates, modalities, and provider signatures.
If both implant failure and neural compression are present, either indication satisfies the criteria; however, all associated documentation must be submitted.
Behavioral health clearance is required when a documented psychosocial disorder exists; a clearance note from a qualified mental health professional must be provided.
Documentation required: Operative report of the original lumbar disc arthroplasty, including level(s) and device details.
Post‑operative plain radiographs, CT, or MRI report demonstrating implant position and any evidence of failure (malposition, subsidence, loosening, fracture, etc.).
MRI or CT report showing neural element compression at the same level (e.g., recurrent disc herniation, facet hypertrophy, osteophytes).
Comprehensive clinical note detailing patient‑reported symptoms (pain scores, functional limitations) and duration of symptoms.
Objective physical examination note documenting neurologic findings correlating with imaging.
Records of conservative management: physical therapy notes (minimum 6 weeks), medication logs, and/or epidural steroid injection reports.
Cotinine test result (serum, saliva, or urine) with date performed and result value.
Behavioral health evaluation or clearance note (if applicable), including diagnosis and treatment status.
Smoking cessation documentation (e.g., counseling notes, nicotine replacement therapy records) if patient is a former smoker.
Signed surgeon’s operative plan indicating fusion with or without decompression and justification based on the above criteria.
